System architecture

How the pieces connect

One Next.js app for every role. Data goes through lib/live.ts stores, which become Firestore listeners. Money is always recalculated on the server.

NeedServiceNotes
Owner loginFirebase Auth — Phone OTP2-step on new device via WhatsApp code
Staff / Sub Admin loginCloud Function staffLoginPIN hash check → custom token {rid, oid, role}
DataCloud FirestoreOffline persistence on — billing works without internet
Photos, bill photosCloud StorageDish galleries, supplier bills
KOT routing, stock, loyalty, nightly AICloud FunctionsFirestore triggers + scheduled
Push to captainsFirebase Cloud Messaging"T4 ready", new QR group
SaaS subscriptionsRazorpay / UPI AutoPayWebhook updates restaurants/{rid}.billing
HostingFirebase App Hosting or VercelPWA — Add to Home Screen
Roles & hierarchy

Four access levels, one chain of control

Super Admin runs the platform. Each client has one owner (Client Admin) for all outlets, a Sub Admin per outlet, and staff inside outlets. Customers don't log in; they verify their phone once.

Super Admin

You. /admin. Every restaurant, plan, trial, payment.

Client Admin

Restaurant owner. role: owner. All outlets, billing, payouts.

Client Sub Admin

Runs one outlet. role: subadmin + outletIds.

Staff

Only the boxes ticked for them. Face + PIN.

Customer

Guest at the table. QR → OTP once.

Groups and shared tables (restaurants)

New phone = new group

Own bill. Friends join with a 4-digit code valid 10 minutes (share on WhatsApp).

Printed QR never changes

Encodes only the table + fixed token. Print once. Protection happens on the order.

Stops home orders

First order of a new group needs one staff tap. OTP phone on every order. Off outside hours.

Shared tables

T6 can hold Party A and Party B — separate orders, KOT labels (T6 · B) and bills.

Visit id

Each sitting gets a new visitId, so yesterday's phone can't rejoin a finished bill.

Optional location check

At first order only. Off by default — some guests refuse location.

Role 3 · Client Sub Admin

Outlet manager — one outlet only

Created by the owner in Members & access: role Sub admin, one or more outlets, and the boxes they get. Runs their outlet and its staff.

Can do (own outlet)

  • Everything ticked for them (default: all 17 boxes)
  • Add, edit, pause and remove staff of their outlet
  • Tick boxes for those staff — only boxes they have themselves
  • Outlet settings: UPI ID, ordering, printers

Cannot do

  • See other outlets or their staff
  • Edit the owner or other Sub Admins
  • Plan, renewal, outlets, restaurant details

Firestore structure

Collections (multi-tenant)

Everything for a client lives under restaurants/{rid}, so one rule isolates each client.

plans/{planId}                         name, monthly, yearly, features[], limits{}
restaurants/{rid}                      name, ownerUid, plan, status, renewsAt, billing{}
  members/{uid}                        name, phone, role(owner|subadmin|staff), title,
                                       outletIds[], perms[], pinHash, active
  outlets/{oid}                        name, address, businessType, upi, payFirst, gstin
    categories/{cid}                   name, icon (order = guest side bar)
    menuItems/{mid}                    name, categoryId, price, diet, station, available, spice,
                                       options[], photos[], recipe[]
    tables/{tid}                       name, zone, seats, qrToken, visitId, reservedAt, parties[]
    guestSessions/{sid}                tableId, visitId, partyId, deviceId
    orders/{orderId}                   number, type, channel, tableId, partyId, guestPhone,
                                       payPreference, prepaid[], payments[], paymentLog[], lines[], status
    kots/{kotId}                       orderId, station, lines[], status      ← kitchen listens here
    ingredients/{iid}                  name, unit, stock, par, costPerUnit, supplierId
    stockMoves/{id}                    ingredientId, qty(+/-), reason, ref
    suppliers/{sid}   purchaseOrders/{poId}
    customers/{phone}                  name, verified, source, optIn, visits, spend, points, tier
      bills/{orderId}
    feedback/{fid}   campaigns/{cid}   expenses/{eid}
    shifts/{id}   attendance/{id}   payroll/{month}
    dayCloses/{yyyy-mm-dd}             expected, counted, variance, by
    insights/{yyyy-mm-dd}              pulse{text, actions[]}, forecast{}, alerts[]
platform/stats                         MRR, counts — for /admin (written by functions)
Cloud Functions

Server-side jobs

Security & tenancy

Security rules

The same checks run on the server: token claims decide what each person can read and write.

Super Admin
platform: true
Client Admin
rid, role: owner
Sub Admin
rid, outletIds, perms
Customer
guestOrders only
function isOwner(rid)      { return request.auth.token.rid == rid && request.auth.token.role == 'owner'; }
function canOutlet(rid, oid) {
  return request.auth.token.rid == rid &&
         (request.auth.token.role == 'owner' || oid in request.auth.token.outletIds);
}
function hasPerm(p) { return request.auth.token.role == 'owner' || p in request.auth.token.perms; }

// members of an outlet: owner, or a sub admin with "team" for that outlet (staff only)
match /restaurants/{rid}/members/{uid} {
  allow write: if isOwner(rid) || (hasPerm('team') && request.resource.data.role == 'staff'
    && request.resource.data.outletIds.hasOnly(request.auth.token.outletIds)
    && request.resource.data.perms.hasOnly(request.auth.token.perms));
}

// restaurant-level docs (plan, billing, members): owner only
match /restaurants/{rid} {
  allow read:  if request.auth.token.rid == rid;
  allow write: if isOwner(rid);
}

// everything inside an outlet: owner, or a Sub Admin / staff assigned to it
match /restaurants/{rid}/outlets/{oid}/{document=**} {
  allow read, write: if canOutlet(rid, oid);
}

// money is never trusted from the client
match /restaurants/{rid}/outlets/{oid}/orders/{id} {
  allow update: if canOutlet(rid, oid)
    && !request.resource.data.diff(resource.data).affectedKeys().hasAny(['totals','payments']);
}

// Super Admin: read-only support view, every action audited
match /{path=**} { allow read: if request.auth.token.platform == true; }

Roadmap & decisions

Next steps to finish

Swap mock data for Firebase

  1. npm i firebase, add lib/firebase.ts (config in .env.local)
  2. Re-implement each function in lib/repo.ts with Firestore (onSnapshot for orders, tables, kitchen)
  3. Replace useState(repo.x()) with a hook like useCollection("orders", …)
  4. Replace demo toast(...) actions with real writes
  5. Move plan checks and access rules into Firestore rules + Cloud Functions
